11 Custom Claude Automations in Field Marketing

Collette Ijeoma is transforming regional marketing at SAP UKI with AI — building automations that handle everything from campaign briefs to event follow-ups.

By Chris O'Hara · August 2026 · 5 min read

When most field marketers are still debating whether to use AI for basic tasks, Collette Ijeoma has already built an entire automation ecosystem. Her approach offers a masterclass in pragmatic AI adoption.

Collette Ijeoma

Field Marketing Lead, SAP UKI
11 Custom Claude Automations Built

Collette Ijeoma leads Field Marketing for SAP in the UKI (UK & Ireland) region. Field marketing is one of the most operationally complex roles in B2B — you're running events, coordinating with sales teams, producing regional content, and managing budgets, all while trying to maintain brand consistency with global campaigns.

Most field marketers respond to this complexity by working longer hours. Collette responded by building systems.

"Every time I found myself doing the same task more than twice, I asked: can Claude do this for me? The answer was usually yes — if I could structure the inputs clearly enough."
— Collette Ijeoma

The Automation Portfolio

Over the past several months, Collette has built 11 distinct automations using Claude Projects — each one addressing a specific pain point in her field marketing workflow. What makes her approach distinctive isn't the technology; it's the discipline of starting with the problem.

Collette's 11 Claude Automations

  • Campaign Brief Generator — Produces structured briefs from sales inputs and campaign goals
  • Event Follow-Up Sequences — Creates personalized outreach for different attendee segments
  • Regional Content Localizer — Adapts global content for UK/Ireland market nuances
  • Budget Tracker & Forecaster — Analyzes spend patterns and projects quarterly outcomes
  • Sales Enablement Summarizer — Distills long product docs into field-ready talking points
  • Competitive Alert Processor — Synthesizes market signals into actionable insights
  • Partner Co-Marketing Coordinator — Generates joint campaign frameworks with partner inputs
  • Event ROI Calculator — Models expected vs. actual performance metrics
  • Lead Qualification Scorer — Applies consistent criteria to event leads
  • Webinar Content Repurposer — Transforms recordings into blogs, social posts, and emails
  • Quarterly Business Review Prep — Structures QBR materials from raw data

The Build vs. Buy Decision

Collette could have waited for IT to provision tools. She could have requested budget for specialized marketing automation platforms. Instead, she recognized that Claude Projects gave her the flexibility to build exactly what she needed — without procurement cycles or vendor lock-in.

Insight 1

Start with Problems, Not Tools

Each automation began with a specific pain point. The tool choice came second.

Insight 2

Structure Before Scale

Getting the inputs right matters more than the AI's capabilities. Garbage in, garbage out.

Insight 3

Document Everything

Each automation has clear documentation — anyone on the team can use them.

Insight 4

Iterate in Public

Sharing wins (and failures) with the broader team accelerates learning for everyone.

Regional Impact

The numbers tell part of the story: campaign turnaround time cut by 60%, event follow-up completion rates up 3x, and consistent quality across all regional outputs. But the bigger impact is what Collette does with the time she's freed up.

Instead of drowning in operational tasks, she now spends more time on strategic work: building relationships with key accounts, developing regional partnerships, and contributing to global campaign strategy. The automations handle the execution; she focuses on the judgment calls that still require human insight.

Lessons for Field Marketers

Collette's approach offers a template for any field marketer looking to adopt AI pragmatically:

  • Audit your repetitive tasks — What do you do weekly that follows a similar pattern each time?
  • Define clear inputs and outputs — AI works best when you know exactly what goes in and what should come out
  • Start small, prove value — One successful automation builds credibility for the next
  • Share your wins — Other team members are facing similar challenges; your solutions can scale
  • Keep humans in the loop — Automations handle drafts; you handle decisions

The Bottom Line

Collette Ijeoma isn't waiting for permission to transform her role. She's not waiting for IT to deploy tools or for marketing leadership to mandate AI adoption. She's building the future of field marketing herself — one automation at a time.

That's the posture that separates PMMs who will thrive in the AI era from those who will be disrupted by it. The tools are available to everyone. The question is who's willing to do the work of building systems that actually leverage them.
